label: Balanced — within states
description: Representation-grouping scheme built with the same population max/min-factor method as 'balanced' (amendment A3.1), but with an added hard constraint: no grouping's member cultural units may span more than one country (amendment A4.1). This is stricter than 'balanced', which merges some undersized units across a state border by affinity (e.g. Moldova into a Romanian grouping, Iceland/Greenland/Faroe into a Norwegian one) to hit the <=7 target. Honest trade-off: small sovereign states with no larger domestic partner to merge with (Iceland, Malta, Cyprus, Slovenia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Luxembourg), plus Greenland and the Faroe Islands (non-sovereign constituent countries of the Kingdom of Denmark, but similarly unable to merge upward at this dataset's country-code granularity), cannot be folded into any grouping without crossing a border, so they sit outside the factor calculation as their own 'sovereign_floor' entries -- structurally unable to merge upward, not merely special_status. The two pre-existing special_status clusters that already crossed borders in the balanced scheme (Alpine Microstates, Crown Dependencies) stay unchanged as factor_exempt (consistent with 'specials stay as marked'); no new cross-border factor_exempt cluster was introduced -- Greenland/Faroe went to sovereign_floor instead, so the border-crossing factor_exempt set remains exactly the two the task named. The resulting 'computed_factor' (population max/min across the remaining non-exempt, non-sovereign_floor groupings) is reported honestly rather than forced to <=7 -- comparing it against affinity-66's and balanced's computed_factor IS the argument for or against allowing cross-border representation merging.

groupings.name: Vienna–Eastern Austria
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton; Vienna's metropolitan and Pannonian weight justifies standalone representation like other large-country capitals (Madrid, Budapest, Paris). (ported unchanged from the 'balanced' scheme for amendment A4.1's balanced-national scheme: this grouping was already single-country and required no split.)

groupings.name: Austria outside Vienna (and Vorarlberg)
groupings.rationale: The non-capital, non-Vorarlberg Austrian Länder combined into one balanced-scheme grouping (4.64M); individually none of Styria, Carinthia, Tyrol, Salzburg or Upper Austria clears the ~2.6M representation floor set by the largest single-unit grouping (London), so they stay merged even though each keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity. Styria and Carinthia sit together inside this grouping by explicit affinity (their pairing is separately endorsed); Carinthia's contested southward alignment is offered as an alternative to the Slovenia-Croatia grouping. (ported unchanged from the 'balanced' scheme for amendment A4.1's balanced-national scheme: this grouping was already single-country and required no split.)

(ported unchanged from the 'balanced' scheme for amendment A4.1's balanced-national scheme: this grouping was already single-country and required no split.)

groupings.rationale: French-speaking Romandie (1.7M) also falls under the representation floor alone; paired with Central-Eastern Switzerland's Alpine cantons (Graubünden and neighbors, which border both Romandie and Ticino) as a population-balancing grouping and Ticino's alternative home. (ported unchanged from the 'balanced' scheme for amendment A4.1's balanced-national scheme: this grouping was already single-country and required no split.)

groupings.name: Greenland
groupings.rationale: Greenland (GL) is a self-governing constituent country of the Kingdom of Denmark (Rigsfaellesskabet) rather than a fully sovereign UN member state, but at this dataset's country-code granularity it is its own atomic unit (GL, distinct from DK), structurally unable to merge upward within its 'state' without crossing a border. In the balanced scheme it merged cross-border into Norway & North Atlantic for population balance; balanced-national disallows that, and rather than introduce a THIRD cross-border factor_exempt cluster beyond the two the task named (alpine-microstates, crown-dependencies), it sits alone here as a single-country sovereign_floor entry -- functionally identical treatment (excluded from computed_factor, cannot merge without crossing a border) even though 'sovereign' is a slight stretch of terminology for a constituent country rather than an independent state.

groupings.name: Wallonia
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme, Wallonia merged cross-border with Luxembourg (grp-b-benelux-francophone) for population balance. Balanced-national keeps every grouping single-country: Wallonia (BE) stands alone -- its own population (3.66M) needs no further domestic merge partner within Belgium (Flanders and Brussels are already their own groupings) -- and Luxembourg (LU) becomes its own sovereign_floor entry instead of merging across the Belgian border.

groupings.name: Sicily-Sardinia
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme these merged cross-border with Malta (grp-b-it-isole-malta) for population balance. Balanced-national keeps Sicily+Sardinia as a single-country Italian grouping (6.39M) and moves Malta to its own sovereign_floor entry instead of merging across the Italy-Malta border.

groupings.name: Croatia
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme Croatia's four units merged cross-border with Slovenia (grp-b-slovenia-croatia) for population balance. Balanced-national unites all of Croatia (3.87M) into one single-country grouping -- it is already the whole state, so no further domestic merge is available or needed -- and moves Slovenia to its own sovereign_floor entry instead of merging across the Croatia-Slovenia border.

groupings.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme, Bosnia's three entities (Federation BiH, Republika Srpska, Brcko District -- kept as separate parliament-rule cultural units) were part of the cross-border grp-b-western-balkans cluster. Balanced-national unites all of Bosnia and Herzegovina (3.54M) into one single-country grouping instead.

groupings.name: Serbia
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme, Serbia's two units were part of the cross-border grp-b-western-balkans cluster. Balanced-national unites all of Serbia (6.44M) into one single-country grouping instead.

groupings.name: Wallachia-Bucharest & Moldavia-Dobrogea
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme these two Romanian units merged cross-border with the Republic of Moldova (grp-b-ro-wallachia-moldavia-md) for population balance -- an explicitly disclosed cross-border representation bloc. Balanced-national keeps Romania's own Wallachia+Moldavia-Dobrogea units together as a single-country grouping (12.72M) and moves the Republic of Moldova to its own sovereign_floor entry instead.

groupings.name: Norway (mainland)
groupings.rationale: In the balanced scheme, mainland Norway merged with Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands (grp-b-norway-north-atlantic) on shared Old Norse realm history. Balanced-national unites mainland Norway's five units into one single-country grouping (5.52M) instead; Iceland, Greenland and the Faroe Islands each become their own sovereign_floor entries (see above) rather than merging across the border.
